AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's shared verdict, copied not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (battle_friend.py:25-29, `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, BattlewornDummyTimeLimitPower, 3)`). Same observable today on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38, relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53, relics/vambrace.py:26-40 and relics/paels_legion.py:36-43, and all four gate on `target is self.player` / `applier is self.player` / `card is not None`, which a self-applied cardless starting power cannot satisfy; (b) HP-roll inversion -- only IllusionPower mentions max_hp and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581); (c) roll ordering -- `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op. Rule 7: that rationale cites four relic files and powers.py which this record does NOT hash. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic/potion/power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. Escalation check per SHARED-FINDINGS section 2: self-applied, reads nothing from hooks.combat -- shared verdict fits. Note the applier is NULL on BOTH sides here (BattleFriendV1/2/3.cs:35 passes null; battle_friend.py:29 omits it), so this is the one unit family in the batch with no applier divergence. **CORRECTION TO A TOOL, REPORTED NOT FIXED:** `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py ctor-order` flags `__battle_friend` as 'C# model has NO AfterAddedToRoom override'. That is an artifact of the roster mis-resolution (SHARED-FINDINGS section 5) -- the probe resolves `__battle_friend` to a nonexistent BattleFriend.cs and therefore finds no overrides at all. All three real C# files DO override AfterAddedToRoom, at BattleFriendV1.cs:33-36, BattleFriendV2.cs:33-36 and BattleFriendV3.cs:33-36, each applying BattlewornDummyTimeLimitPower 3m. Section 2's shared verdict therefore applies unchanged and no escalation is needed.

GenerateMoveStateMachine (protected; add.rationale: Node-by-node against BattleFriendV1.cs:26-31. ONE MoveState, `MoveState("NOTHING_MOVE", _ => Task.CompletedTask)` -- an empty delegate and no intents -- whose FollowUpState is itself, registered as the single-element list and used as the initial state. The sim's shared base builds exactly that (battle_friend.py:31-36: `nothing.follow_up = nothing`, `MonsterMoveStateMachine([nothing], nothing)`, perform delegate `lambda ctx: None`). The dummy never acts on either side; the fight is a timer. No branch state on either side (EXECUTED, `py audit/tools/monster_probes_b06.py branch-args`). The machine is byte-identical in all three C# files, which is exactly why the sim hoists it here.

guards.what: HOW THIS RECORD RESOLVES ITS MISSING C# COUNTERPART, and the name_overrides entry it needs
guards.rationale: `py audit/tools/harness.py roster monster` reports `UNMATCHED monster/__battle_friend -> expected src\Core\Models\Monsters\BattleFriend.cs`: the sim's leading-underscore intermediate base (battle_friend.py:16-36) has no C# class of that name, and the real files are BattleFriendV1.cs / V2.cs / V3.cs. This record chooses the CONCRETE FILE option over the `sim_only` option, and the reason is a fidelity one rather than a convenience one: a `sim_only` record must carry a rationale naming why there is no C# counterpart, and that claim would be FALSE here. `_BattleFriend` is not a sim invention -- it is the exact common part of three real C# classes. Its two members, `__init__`'s BattlewornDummyTimeLimitPower 3 and `build_machine`'s single self-looping NOTHING_MOVE, are byte-identical at BattleFriendV1.cs:26-36, BattleFriendV2.cs:26-36 and BattleFriendV3.cs:26-36. Declaring it sim-only would leave the shared machine and the shared starting power audited against no source at all. Pointing it at V1 (with V2 and V3 hashed as extra_sources so a divergence between the three cannot go stale) audits every shared line against real C#, and the three per-variant members that DO differ -- MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp, SetupSkins -- are each verdicted in the subclass records that own them. **RECOMMENDED `audit/tools/name_overrides.json` ENTRY (relic stream owns that file; not applied here):** `"monster/__battle_friend": "src/Core/Models/Monsters/BattleFriendV1.cs"`. That single line makes `harness.py roster monster` resolve, makes `harness.py skeleton monster/__battle_friend` generate the same five hooks this record fills by hand, and fixes the false 'C# model has NO AfterAddedToRoom override' flag that `monster_probes.py ctor-order` currently prints for this unit. The sibling row, `monster/__cultist`, is another batch's to resolve.

guards.what: NOTHING_MOVE carries no intents in C#
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-30 (tier-2 campaign): (Task 28.) 'No intent' is now expressible: monsters/base.py gained MoveType.NONE and Intent.none(); all 4 Battle Friend dummy sites construct it, mirroring the empty `params AbstractIntent[]` in BattleFriendV1/V2/V3.cs:28. No consumer tests MoveType.NONE (full_env.py's ten flag checks exclude it, so the dummies encode all-zero flags; test/run.py renders 'None' safely); every other monster's constructed intents are byte-identical (defaulted fields only, verified by a 321-site grep). MoveType.UNKNOWN stays reserved for state_machine.py's UNSET_MOVE sentinel. Witness: test/test_monster_tier_families.py::TestNoIntentUnrepresentable.  The text it replaced read: BattleFriendV1/2/3.cs:28 constructs the MoveState with NO intents at all -- the `AbstractIntent[] intents` params array is empty, so the dummy telegraphs nothing. The sim substitutes `Intent(MoveType.UNKNOWN)` (battle_friend.py:32-34). Same mechanism as the StatusIntent-count loss on the_insatiable and aeonglass: the sim's Intent (monsters/base.py:36-59) collapses a C# AbstractIntent[] and cannot express 'no intent'. monster_state_machine's scope boundary item 2 records the whole mapping as audited by no seam. NOT LIVE: nothing in the sim distinguishes UNKNOWN from absent (there is no empty Intent), so no ported consumer can observe it. Named trigger: an observation or replay consumer that renders the intent list, or any content gating on `MonsterModel.IntendsToAttack` (MonsterModel.cs:241-245), which reads the intent list and has no sim counterpart.
